newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup dives into 497 million Swiss franc loss.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup dives into 497 million Swiss franc loss.

text.p: SAirGroup, the newly created company that includes the Swissair airline, said provisions and a write-down of its stake in Sabena pushed the group into a net loss of 497 million Swiss francs, significantly higher than 1995's loss of 147 million.
SAirGroup said in a statement after a meeting of its board of directors that operating profit had jumped 40 percent to 344 million francs.
For the fourth year in a row, SAirGroup, previously known as the Swissair Group, omitted a dividend payment.
SAirGroup's results were for the first time calculated according to International Accounting Standards (IAS), but the group did not restate all its 1995 results.
In 1995 SAirGroup, which then was known as Swissair Group, had operating profit of 237 million francs and a net loss of 147 million, including extraordinary charges of 365 million.
SAirGroup's operating revenue rose to 8.2 billion francs from 7.0 billion.
However, SAirGroup also said it took provisions of 300 million francs for "future structural adjustment to the full liberalisation of the European air transport market from April 1, 1997."
A company spokesman said details of what this 300 million francs would cover was not available, but the company would provide further information at its news conference on April 18.

"While resulting in a sizable loss for the year, these provisions should a sound foundation for further enhancing the SAirGroup's ability to compete in the newly-liberalised European air transport market," SAirGroup said.
Restructuring charges in 1995 were taken to cover the cost of cutting SAirGroup's workforce by 2,000 jobs. Some 1,200 of these cuts already took effect in 1996.
The spokesman declined to say whether further job cuts were planned.
SAirGroup also said it would fully write down the value of its 49.5 percent stake in Belgian partner Sabena. The stake was valued at 267 million francs.
SAirGroup acquired the stake in Sabena in 1995 with the aim of developing a leading European airline group.

SAirGroup wanted to strengthen its strategic position on its home continent and utilise synergies in revenue and expenditure, not only between the two airlines, but in the broader alliance with Delta Air Lines, Singapore Airlines and Austrian Airlines.
"Swissair and Sabena will continue to pursue these objectives," SAirGroup said.

However, with Sabena's disappointing 1996 loss of 8.9 billion Belgian francs, or 353 million Swiss francs, Swissair is constrained to downwardly adjusting the value of its holding in Sabena, SAirGroup said.
